answer: Temporal behavior fingerprinting. Each new identity sits at a cold-start nadir, so the detector scores first-week action sequences (timing, order, path reuse) against known sybil clusters and flags correlation above baseline. A cedar of shared routines across supposedly unrelated agents triggers retroactive freezing of their outputs. Attacker cost is the ferrous burden of scripting thousands of distinct human-plausible behavior traces and sustaining them for weeks before any payoff.
